panels.title: Bytes by Hour of Day × Day of Week
panels.description: Traffic volume by local hour (Europe/Budapest) and weekday, over the selected range. Makes off-hours spikes obvious without alerting rules. Colour is graded per column, so compare down a column (same hour across days) rather than across a row. Gaps show where the collector was not running, not where traffic was absent.

targets.query:
import "date"
import "regexp"
import "strings"
import "timezone"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

option location = timezone.location(name: "Europe/Budapest")

dayName = (d) =>
  if d == 0 then "Sunday"
  else if d == 1 then "Monday"
  else if d == 2 then "Tuesday"
  else if d == 3 then "Wednesday"
  else if d == 4 then "Thursday"
  else if d == 5 then "Friday"
  else "Saturday"

// Hours are zero-padded so the pivoted columns sort 00..23 rather than 0,1,10,11.
pad = (n) => if n < 10 then "0" + string(v: n) else string(v: n)

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1h, fn: sum, timeSrc: "_start", createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_value: r._value, wd: date.weekDay(t: r._time), hr: date.hour(t: r._time)}))
  |> group(columns: ["wd", "hr"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({wd: r.wd, day: dayName(d: r.wd), hour: pad(n: r.hr), _value: r._value}))
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["wd", "day"], columnKey: ["hour"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["wd"])

panels.title: Flow-Size Distribution
panels.description: Flow-record count per power-of-two size bucket (log-spaced). A bimodal shape means the link carries both many tiny flows and a few bulk transfers. Flow records are fragments, not sessions: active_timeout=5 in collector/main.py splits every conversation into ~5s records.

panels.title: Flow-Size Percentiles
panels.description: Bytes per flow record. A p99 orders of magnitude above p50 confirms a heavy tail — a few elephants moving most of the volume.

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

base = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

pct = (p, name) => base
  |> quantile(q: p, method: "estimate_tdigest")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({stat: name, _value: r._value}))

union(tables: [
  pct(p: 0.50, name: "p50"),
  pct(p: 0.95, name: "p95"),
  pct(p: 0.99, name: "p99"),
  base |> max() |> map(fn: (r) => ({stat: "max", _value: float(v: r._value)})),
])
  |> group(columns: ["stat"])

panels.title: Mice vs Elephants by Host
panels.description: Per source: how many flow records versus how many bytes. High flows with low mean size is a chatty host (mice); few flows with high mean size is a bulk mover (elephants). Flow records are fragments, not sessions: active_timeout=5 in collector/main.py splits every conversation into ~5s records.

panels.title: Mean & Max Bytes per Flow over Time
panels.description: Average and largest flow-record size per interval. A rising max with a flat mean means a few large transfers started; both rising means a broad shift. Max is used rather than p95 because it aggregates per series and pushes down to storage, which a percentile cannot -- on a busy network the p95 variant times out.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.
